markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (43%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
Reliability is flagged at 4% [F6]; Normal, Benign and Invasive all remain in the 90% set.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 43%, Invasive 32%, Benign 13% | Weak separation |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign, Invasive | Three classes unresolved |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.04 / 68th percentile | Input flagged suspect |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models disagree on top class |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 Normal | Neighbors mostly disagree |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 9, 10, 11) · ↑ invasive · Strongest concept association with invasive carcinoma [F2] · Validated
- **Normal lobules** (regions 0, 1, 3) · ↓ invasive · Concept model links it to lower invasive likelihood · Unreliable
- **Tumor necrosis** (regions 4, 9, 10) · ↑ invasive · Modest invasive association; spot check poor · Unreliable
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 8, 9, 10) · ↑ invasive · Small invasive association in the lower row · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (−0.005 to 0.007): not shown to reflect the classifier; leans on Unreliable normal lobules and necrosis.

## Could be wrong if
- Image quality is poor (reliability 4%), so every probability here may be off.
- Regions 8–11 score 87–100% invasive individually, yet the top class is Normal.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 8–11**: confirm infiltrating tumor versus benign stroma.
2. **Regions 4, 9, 10**: verify necrosis; its concept spot check was poor.
3. **Regions 0, 1, 3**: verify normal lobules; its spot check was 0/20.
